## TL;DR

This task improves first-run and failure guidance on Work and Agents. The Work board now distinguishes a successfully empty project from a failed request, offers task creation and retry actions, and keeps these panels in the normal page flow outside the responsive board columns. A failed load remains visible when a status filter is active. The Agents page points projects with no configured roles toward the built-in agent choices. Preview fixtures and regression tests cover the conditional states.

## Work and rationale

The Work store now preserves an initial board request error separately from loading and task data. That distinction matters because an empty array can mean either “the request succeeded and there are no tasks” or “the request did not load.” Work uses the error state for a clear server connection message and Retry action; a successful refresh clears the error. On a successful empty response, the board offers a first-task prompt and opens the existing create-task flow.

The first review found that both prompts were direct children of `.board`. That container is a flex row on wide screens and a three-column grid below 1250px, so its layout rules squeezed the callouts alongside task columns. I moved the sections into the Work page flow immediately before the board. They retain their full available width at wide, tablet and phone layouts, and the columns remain governed by the existing responsive board layout. The error section is now conditional on the board view and load result only; it no longer disappears when a status filter is present. The empty-board prompt remains suppressed for filtered views because a filtered zero count does not mean the project itself is empty.

The Agents page checks for projects with no configured roles and links directly to the built-in agent choices. Its `agents:empty` preview fixture creates this visual state without changing saved configuration. Work uses `work:empty` and `work:failedLoad` fixtures. Tests verify the fixtures and the Agents config behavior, while the mobile queue tests cover the initial load error and successful retry.

## Approaches tried

For the initial QA pass, I started the auth-less server from this task worktree and exercised the Work and Agents views at 1280×900 and 375×812 using Playwright WebKit. The empty and failed-load Work fixtures and the empty Agents fixture showed their intended messages at both sizes; the document width matched each viewport and I observed no page or console errors. I also intercepted the live board request to fail, verified the user-facing server guidance, clicked Retry, then allowed the request to succeed and observed tasks return at both widths.

For the review findings, I used component tests to verify the two guidance sections are outside the board container and that the load-error panel remains visible alongside an active Ready filter. The work-queue visibility suite passes with these regression cases included.

## Challenges and blockers

The computer-use browser bridge did not expose viewport controls or console output, so I switched to the repository's Playwright WebKit runner for responsive and error-path checks. The initial scoped check found a formatter issue in `AgentsView.vue`; I ran `bun run fmt` and reran the check. For review round 2, the focused work-queue test suite passed all 11 tests. The required changed-path RepoOS check then passed: remote changed-path tests, build, format, lint, CSS and contrast guards, and UI smoke completed successfully.

## Key learnings

Conditional guidance should be structurally separate from a responsive collection's layout container. Styling a wide callout inside a flex/grid list is fragile because responsive column rules will treat it like an item. Also, filters change the subset being viewed, not whether the underlying request succeeded; transport errors should remain visible regardless of the current filter. A real request interception complements fixtures by proving that retry recovers after a failed response.
